claims.text: A large permanent vacuole, bounded by a single membrane called the tonoplast, is a feature of mature plant cells. It contains cell sap, stores sugars, ions and pigments, and its pressure on the cell wall keeps the cell firm; the tonoplast controls which substances pass between the sap and the cytoplasm. Plasmodesmata are narrow channels through adjacent plant cell walls, lined by cell surface membrane, which link the cytoplasm of neighbouring cells.

claims.text: A mitochondrion has an envelope of two membranes; the inner one is folded into cristae that surround the fluid matrix. claims.text: Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis (translation). Those in the cytoplasm and on the rough endoplasmic reticulum are 80S; those inside mitochondria and chloroplasts are the smaller 70S type. Rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) is a network of flattened, membrane-bound sacs studded with ribosomes, and the proteins made on those ribosomes enter the sacs and are carried onwards. Smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) has no ribosomes and is where lipids are made and processed.

claims.text: The Golgi body is a stack of flattened, membrane-bound sacs. It receives proteins in vesicles from the RER, modifies them (for example by adding carbohydrate groups), packages them into vesicles, and sends them on, either to the cell surface membrane for secretion or to form lysosomes. A lysosome is a small, round, single-membrane sac containing hydrolytic enzymes that digest worn-out organelles, material taken in by the cell, and invading microbes. The route of a secreted protein is therefore gene in the nucleus, copy to mRNA, synthesis on ribosomes on RER, transport in vesicles to the Golgi body, modification and packaging, then vesicles to the cell surface membrane.

claims.text: Centrioles are a pair of short hollow cylinders of microtubules found next to the nucleus of animal cells; they organise the spindle during nuclear division, and the cells of flowering plants generally lack them. Cilia are hair-like projections of the cell surface membrane, each containing microtubules, which beat to move fluid or mucus across a surface. Microvilli are much smaller, finger-like folds of the cell surface membrane that do not beat; they increase the surface area for absorption or secretion.

claims.text: To make a temporary wet mount, first place a drop of water on a clean slide. Peel a thin layer of tissue, such as the inner epidermis of an onion scale, with forceps (or gently scrape the inside of the cheek with a clean cotton bud for cheek cells), and lay it flat in the drop. Add a drop of stain, such as iodine solution for onion or methylene blue for cheek cells. Lower a coverslip onto the specimen at an angle, using a mounted needle, and blot any excess liquid from the edge with filter paper. For animal cells a drop of dilute saline is gentler than water, which can make the cells swell.

claims.text: The specimen must be thin, ideally one cell thick, so that light passes through it and cells do not overlap. A stain is added because most cells are almost colourless and the stain gives contrast between structures such as the nucleus and the cytoplasm. The coverslip is lowered at an angle so that air bubbles are not trapped, and it holds the specimen flat and keeps it moist; the slide is not allowed to dry out because dry cells shrivel and distort. Cheek cells are the learner's own: used slides and cotton buds go into disinfectant, and slides are not shared.

claims.text: Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells both have a cell surface membrane, cytoplasm, ribosomes and DNA. claims.text: ATP is the immediate energy currency of the cell. When its terminal phosphate group is removed by hydrolysis, ATP becomes ADP and phosphate and releases a small amount of energy that the cell can use directly for processes such as active transport, protein synthesis, muscle contraction and cell division. ADP and phosphate are joined again to make ATP using energy from respiration or from light, so a cell keeps only a small store and recycles it continuously.
